newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on trade figures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on trade figures.

text.p: Mexican peso contracts firmed to close at their strongest levels since February 27 on Wednesday, helped by positive trade figures, after zigzagging through the session, dealers said.
The Financial Ministry said that Mexico had posted a preliminary trade surplus of $182 million in June.
"Figures like this show that things are on the right track," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended the session 0.8 and 1.0 centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8280/7.8330 and 7.8250/7.8300 per dollar.
The figures compared with an average surplus of $165 million predicted by 12 financial firms in the latest Reuters survey.
Another dealer said the peso had also firmed on a stable U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which was meanwhile off 3/32 to yield 6.42 percent.
"There has been some speculation but nothing unusual; players are following the international scene," he said.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade mid-morning 1.0 centavo firmer at 7.8370/7.8410 per dollar.
Dealers placed strong resistance for the 48-hour peso at 7.8000 per dollar.
